source.version_note: Cognition262:106177,available online13May2025. Eight experiments declared exploratory despite preregistration; presented out of collection order. Abstract Study4summary conflicts with main results.

citation.title: Moral psychological exploration of the asymmetry effect in AI-assisted euthanasia decisions

reading.source_scope_note: Human moral-approval ratings of fictional medical scenarios; no model acts,no patient is treated,and no clinical decision or objective ethical correctness is established.
access_limits: All20extracted pages read,including all eight studies,preregistration/exploratory qualification,internal synthesis,discussion and references. Rendered pages9,11,14inspected for Figure2statistics,Study4direction/outcome labels and Study5/6results.

External OSFpreregistrations,full scenario/scale appendices,Figsharedata/scripts and analysis outputs were not opened or rerun. Studies described as replicated without exclusions are authors' reports,not independently reproduced checks.
Crossref metadata verified the Huebner reference's author spelling only. That primary paper and cited books remain unread.

study.overview: Eight experiments; abstracttotalN5837 versus sum of reported analyzedNs5785,unresolved
study.study_1: Human/robotxwithdraw/maintain life support,between-person; English and Czech. Human-minus-robot approval of withdrawal B.76,CI[.48,1.04] and.52,CI[.14,.90]; no detected source contrast for maintaining.
study.study_2: Finnish/English randomized3teams(AI-robot,AI-human,human-human),withdrawal only. Lower approval with more AI; main-text and Figure2contrast statistics differ.
study.study_3: Human/AI recommender x human/robot decision-maker between-person,withdraw/maintain within-person,counterbalanced. Reported full factorial ANOVA residualdf2300 equals2N−8; within-person covariance handling not identified.
study.study_4: Human/robot x4procedures,conscious patient repeatedly requests ending suffering. Six-item outcome revised tofive after inspection. Human-source main effect; withdrawal-only source contrast B.29,CI[-.11,.70],p.15; other source contrasts reported significant.
study.study_5: Human/robot x high/low described competence between-person,withdraw/maintain within-person. High-competence withdrawal contrast B.15,CI[-.07,.37],p.19; maintaining B.47,CI[.24,.71],p<.001.
study.study_6: AI-only,high competence,withdrawal fixed. Explainability wording/algorithm-family condition x reported accuracy77–97%. Approval B.21,CI[.05,.36],p.009 for explainability and.02peraccuracy point,p.007; partialetas.006/.007. No human control.
study.synthesis: Within-paper fixed-effect/meta-regression reuse of earlier data;not another independent study or general external meta-analysis.

summary: Add the now explicitly defined human–robot moral judgment asymmetry as a human judgment-pattern umbrella,not a unique causal mechanism. Its decision-rating outcome differs from generic algorithm-use reluctance,machine generosity penalties,outrage and blame. Preserve conditional effects and substantial source/reporting limits; the conscious-patient and explainability studies do not establish broad disappearance or a fully identified mechanism.

findings.definition: Differences in moral evaluations of otherwise matched decisions attributed to human versus artificial agents.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Direct human observer experiments on fictional human/AI medical decisions; contextual outcome pattern with unresolved reporting and analysis issues,not an identified AI mechanism
findings.ai_proposal: Compare AI-generated moral evaluations of matched actions while varying whether the described actor is human or artificial. Audit whether differences follow relevant capabilities,authority,consent and accountability evidence or merely a source label. Separately measure the human public's approval of AI decisions; neither task alone establishes which judgment is ethically right.
findings.novelty_rationale: Earlier files mentioned an undefined broad asymmetry and it was deferred. This primary article explicitly defines and measures decision evaluation while distinguishing it from general reluctance to use machines. Retain as an umbrella outcome pattern; related narrower effects are not synonyms or multiple independent causal mechanisms.

findings.evidence_scope: Human moral-approval ratings of fictional medical scenarios; no model acts,no patient is treated,and no clinical decision or objective ethical correctness is established. Studies1a/1bfind human-favoring withdrawal contrasts; maintaining support has no detected contrast. Studies2/3vary chain composition; Study4depends on procedure; Study5changes the pattern with described competence. Eight experiments in one article are one cited research paper. Study6has no human comparison and cannot directly test this asymmetry.
findings.boundary: A pattern can favor either source and vary across choices; it is not inherently an irrational double standard. Relevant autonomy,capability,oversight and responsibility differences can justify judgments. Distinguish decision approval,actor suitability,trust,blame,outrage and actual use. Null contrasts are not equivalence; omitted interaction tests do not establish boundary conditions. No real AI moral action or subjective state is demonstrated.

findings.term: Moral decision approval is distinct from algorithm-use reluctance
findings.definition: Rating one assigned AI decision less favorably than a human decision does not alone show refusal to use algorithmic advice or delegate a clinical task.
findings.novelty_rationale: Maintains the distinction that motivates the new umbrella entry instead of merging all human–AI differences into general algorithm aversion.

evidence.quote: decisions – rather than the agents – are evaluated as appropriate

findings.evidence_scope: The article explicitly distinguishes actor-level general aversion from decision-specific moral approval. No actual clinical advice selection or tool-use behavior is observed.
findings.boundary: Approval may depend on justified role and oversight expectations. The withdrawal penalty is not a universal preference for humans in all decisions,as maintaining support and some competence/procedure conditions differ.

findings.term: Competence descriptions change approval but do not prove moral-character mediation
findings.definition: Describing a doctor as precise and praised versus error-prone and unfit changes moral approval,but bundles competence,reputation and expected decision quality.
findings.novelty_rationale: A boundary between competence information and the existing moral-character/intent focus; not an extra independent character mechanism or demonstration that competence equals virtue.

evidence.quote: colleagues praise it for its abilities

findings.evidence_scope: Study5manipulates described high/low competence,not actual task accuracy. Both human and robot approval change; source contrasts shift rather than globally vanish.
findings.boundary: Competence is a relevant reason for medical reliance,not automatically halo. Comparing a significant contrast with a nonsignificant one is not itself a moderation test. No measured mediator establishes why the words changed judgments.

findings.term: Active/passive labels do not isolate omission bias
findings.definition: Withholding treatment,withdrawing it,risky symptom treatment and intended medically assisted death differ in intention,causality,treatment history and patient consent,not only action versus inaction.
findings.novelty_rationale: The paper invokes omission bias secondarily,but its procedure contrasts do not isolate a preference for otherwise identical harms caused by omission.
findings.evidence_scope: Study4changes four substantive procedures for a conscious requesting patient; previous studies concern an unconscious patient's prognosis. Differences can be morally relevant.
findings.boundary: Do not equate all treatment withdrawal with killing or every preference for withholding with a bias. The paper itself notes that classifying ordinary withdrawal as passive euthanasia is contested. No clinical/legal guidance follows from these ratings.

findings.term: Explainability effects are not a replication of an appearance-based moral uncanny valley
findings.definition: Described algorithmic explainability and accuracy can affect approval of a fictional AI decision without manipulating robot appearance or measuring uncanniness.
findings.novelty_rationale: Connects related judgment research while preventing a general AI-source effect from being counted as another direct moral uncanny valley replication.
findings.evidence_scope: Study6holds AI identity and competence fixed,with wording plus algorithm-family differences and reported accuracy. It does not directly estimate a human-versus-AI gap or test an appearance/mind mechanism.
findings.boundary: No evidence here establishes appearance,perceived mind or category competition as the cause. An existing adjusted mind-perception analysis from2023does not rule out all causal mind effects.

methodological_limits: The abstract's analyzed totalN5837does not equal628+301+285+401+1154+830+1089+1097=5785from the eight methods sections. The52participant discrepancy is unresolved;do not guess a corrected sample or assume the100-person pilot explains it.
Study2afinalN285conflicts with161women+148men=309. Study5methodsN1089conflicts with Table2N1088;reported residualdf2170matches2x1089−8,not the table'sN. Clarify actual samples.
Study6says1118recruited and1097retained,a21person or1.9%reduction,while the same paragraph says approximately20%excluded. Initial sample,exclusion rate and finalNneed reconciliation.

Main-text Study2atrend B.81,CI[.39,1.24],F13.78 differs from Figure2B.59,CI[.39,.80],F32.27. Study2bmain B1.04,CI[.68,1.39],F33.39,df398 differs from caption B.75,CI[.51,98],F38.55,df403. The latter interval also omits a decimal. Do not pick one unverified version.

Abstract says asymmetry disappears for active euthanasia including lethal injection. Main Study4results and Figure4show significant human/robot differences for medically assisted death,withholding and risky treatment;only withdrawal is not detected,p.15. Later discussion's only-in-medically-assisted wording also conflicts with those simple source contrasts.

Study4withdrawal estimate B.29,CI[-.11,.70],p.15does not establish equivalence or disappearance. No significant overall interaction is reported. Different significance between procedures is not automatically significant moderation.

Consciousness,explicit request,illness,pain,scenario and procedures change across Study4and other experiments. This comparison cannot isolate patient autonomy or consciousness as a necessary/sufficient causal boundary.

The absence of explicit wishes for a comatose patient does not itself establish that withdrawal violates autonomy. Advance directives,substitute decision authority and clinical indications are not fully represented;the paper suggests DNR/family-consent tests only as future work.

Studies3and5collect two outcome ratings per person,but report full factorial residualdf2300and2170,exactly2N−8. The main text does not identify a participant random effect or repeated-measure covariance correction. Analysis scripts are needed to check whether dependence was handled.

The Study3power rationale claims d.07needs about500pergroup and halves participants because each provides two responses. That is not a sufficient repeated-measure power specification;design correlation and effect-size convention are missing,and the stated independent d calculation is implausible.

All studies are preregistered according to authors,but all are ultimately declared exploratory because original hypotheses did not consistently hold. Collection order is changed for presentation and exclusion criteria were refined. Confirmatory wording must retain that qualification;external registrations were not read.

Study4drops one item after observing treatment-effect differences across included/full samples and inspecting each item's significance. An item not tracking the treatment is not automatically noise. CFAon the same data may reveal invariance issues,but does not make the revised five-item test independent confirmation.
Figure4axis says single-item moral acceptance,while the accompanying results describe a five-item composite after revision. Which outcome is plotted needs clarification.

Study4reports treatment F(1,822)=3.20,p.02although treatment has four levels;the earlier full test has3numeratordf. It also gives F(1,822)=8.51,p.036,inconsistent with the stated df. No guessed p or df correction is substituted.

Study4medically-assisted contrasts have negative B values paired with positive-centered confidence intervals:robot−.35versus[.05,.66],human−.23versus[-.07,.54]. Contrast direction/sign needs reconciliation.

Study3Table1partialeta values do not consistently match F/(F+2300):RecommenderxDMF1.21is printed.005rather than about.0005;RecommenderxDecisionF10.91is printed.000rather than about.0047. Some prose/table estimates also differ.

Study5high-competence withdrawal contrast p.19does not demonstrate equal approval;high competence also shows a human-favoring maintaining-support contrast. The pattern shifts instead of simply proving all asymmetry is removed.
Competence wording bundles precision,work performance,peer praise and job fitness. It is not measured actual diagnostic accuracy,and its effects need not be an irrational moral-character bias.
Study6has AI-only conditions and explicitly acknowledges the missing human comparator. It cannot directly show what fraction of a human–AI asymmetry explainability/accuracy explains.

Study6explains/denies explainability with explicit wording and different algorithm families. Labels such as linear regression versus random forest,neural network,SVMor genetic algorithm are not a universal proof that every instance is transparent/opaque. Algorithm identity,explanation content and framing are bundled.

Study6shows small approval effects,partialetas.006and.007. Its reported coefficient-ratio tradeoff of about12accuracy percentage points is a local model estimate,not a clinical policy recommendation,validated trust calibration or universal substitute for meaningful explanation.

Reported accuracy is a fictional global percentage with no sensitivity,specificity,calibration,base-rate or patient-specific uncertainty. It is presented as better than any senior human doctor,not established real performance. Training-set accuracy is not demonstrated external clinical accuracy.

Fixed future-year2051scenarios,written prognosis and inevitable outcomes do not represent actual consent,legal requirements or bedside decision processes. Public moral approval does not establish medical permissibility or safety.
The six-item morality composite includes praise,rightness,benefit and permissibility;these may vary with source/condition. Reliability alone does not establish the same construct across all studies.

Large exclusions and different recruitment streams limit representativeness. Czech volunteers include science-fiction audiences;Finnish recruitment combines commercial panel,Prolific and snowballing. Three language settings are not three representative cultures or proof universal effects.

The internal synthesis reuses the earlier experiments and is not independent replication. Standardized outcomes/fixed effects and correlated repeated ratings need a clear unit of analysis and covariance specification;within-paper pooling does not resolve primary reporting conflicts.

The internal meta-analysis suggests some approval differences for maintaining support,although individual studies often have null contrasts. This is compatible with higher precision but prevents a blanket claim of no effect without testing practical equivalence.

Multiple simple contrasts,alternative outcomes and exploratory explanations require caution. Inactive/active choices,praise/blame,decisions/agents and patient autonomy are not interchangeable dependent variables.

Kin-selection,evolutionary mismatch,personhood,uniqueness neglect and perceived mind are proposed explanations. The studies do not directly measure all these processes or show that a human/AI source difference is inherently a cognitive error.

Theoretical claims about family permission,unconscious patients and reduced moral distress are not clinical recommendations. No healthcare worker distress,real patient outcome or deployed AI behavior is measured.
External raw data,analysis scripts,registrations and cited primary sources/books remain unread. Metadata verification of Huebner is separate from substantive reading.

cross_paper_learning.finding: The previously deferred broad asymmetry now has an explicit primary definition and direct multi-condition decision-rating experiments. Add a named umbrella pattern with links to the narrower appearance effect,but no claim of a new independent causal explanation.

The original appearance study pools decisions;the later moral uncanny study reverses by decision type;the present source varies action,role and competence. These are contextual judgment patterns,not a single universal machine penalty.

Banks measures responsibility,goodness and perceived mind for scripted responses. The present six-item decision-approval scale is a different outcome;neither can be silently relabeled as blame,outrage or actual actor morality.

Strongly described character/competence can affect ratings without uniquely identifying a character mediator. Different studies and stimulus changes do not isolate sensory realism or patient autonomy.

As with the academic guilt study,headline totals and model summaries require reconciliation before quantitative reuse. Self-report moral outcomes do not establish clinical validity or a causal psychological process.

deferred.reason: Discussed through a cited medical-AI explanation but not separately defined by name or directly measured here. Read Longoni et al.'s primary treatment before adding it.

deferred.term: Command-chain effect as an independent mechanism
deferred.reason: Here it denotes role/team manipulations with several possible explanations,not a uniquely isolated psychological process. Preserve design details under the asymmetry entry.
Approval effects can reflect relevant information rather than an error. Neither general defect label nor underlying mechanism is directly established.
Speculative interpretations,not direct measures or validated novel behaviors in these studies.

source_corrections.correction: Do not repeat that active euthanasia generally removes the source difference. The main text reports human-favoring contrasts for medically assisted death,withholding and risky treatment;withdrawal contrast is nonsignificant,not equivalent.
Eight reported final samples sum5785rather than abstract5837;Study2agendercounts sum309rather thanN285;Study5table/methodsNandStudy6exclusion percentage disagree.
Retain conflicting contrast estimates,dfs,interval signs and outcome labels in review record;no raw-data correction guessed.
Crossref DOI10.1007/s11097-009-9126-6identifies Bryce Huebner,not Heubner. Retain2010issue citation separately from2009online availability;the primary text was not read.

limitations: One named umbrella judgment pattern is added with explicit overlap and uncertainty. This is not another proven AI defect or a unique causal mechanism. Eight experiments and an internal synthesis do not create nine independent papers. No normative edge,clinical recommendation,unread-book claim or annual series is fabricated.
